MASAF/Sicilia register, girth 410cm, height 10m. Giardino Inglese (Piersanti Mattarella Park) is well documented as a public 1851 exotic-plant garden (English Wikipedia), which is good general context but not a source naming this specific tree; searched for a dedicated second source this pass (cefalunews.org, venipedia.it, lasiciliainrete.it, monumentaltrees.com) without success in the time available. venipedia.it 403s automated fetches; cefalunews.org's automated summary garbled the register's girth-cm column into a fake 'years' age for every tree in it (a live example of the units/fields trap BRIEF_RESEARCH.md warns about, do not trust that page's numbers for anything). Worth a browser-session look at monumentaltrees.com's Giardino Inglese pages, which do exist for at least one other tree there (a Ficus macrophylla, https://www.monumentaltrees.com/en/ita/sicily/palermo/4318_giardinoinglese/).

leads.species: Nolina longifolia (Villa Malfitano Whitaker - Via Dante 167)
leads.reason: MASAF register, girth 410cm, height 7m, 58m from pal_004 (a fourth Villa Malfitano specimen alongside the already-published dragon tree, fig and yucca). UPDATE (2026-08-20 verify pass): fetched turismo.cittametropolitana.pa.it's Villa Malfitano garden page directly (already used as a source for pal_013) looking for this specimen; it confirms the garden holds notable Nolina-type plants but names them 'Nolina recurvata e Nolina stricta' rather than 'Nolina longifolia', and 'Nolina recurvata' is itself a historical synonym sometimes used for a different genus (Beaucarnea recurvata, ponytail palm), not confidently the same plant as this register row. So the register (source 1) and this garden page (source 2, general but real) both put a large Nolina-type specimen in this garden, but do not clearly agree on which species, which is a species-identity gap rather than an existence gap. Given the page already carries three exotic/succulent specimens from this one villa, left as a lead rather than pushed through on a rushed species call; a future pass with more time should try to pin down which Nolina/Beaucarnea species this sheet actually is before shipping a fourth Villa Malfitano entry.

MASAF register, girth 240cm, height 28m (unusually tall for its girth, worth a sanity check on a future pass). Villa di Napoli's garden is independently and repeatedly described (Wikipedia, FAI 'Luoghi del Cuore', balarm.it, italiani.it) as holding one of Sicily's largest monumental trees, a Ficus macrophylla with a canopy that dominates much of the garden's northern end, which is a real second source for existence, species and general remarkableness even though none of these give this specific register sheet's own measurements. UPDATE (2026-08-20 verify pass): the villa's own Italian Wikipedia page states the garden is currently closed pending restoration ('Attualmente se ne attende la riapertura da parte delle autorita competenti'), with only occasional reservation-only weekend openings (a 2016 example ran three weekends, 30-minute timed slots). This is not a paid-but-open garden like Villa Malfitano or Villa Tasca; it is a public monument that cannot currently be walked up to on an ordinary afternoon. Left as a lead rather than blocked outright, since the closure is explicitly described as awaiting reopening rather than permanent, and the underlying land is public (Regione Siciliana), not private: revisit if a future pass finds evidence the garden has reopened on regular hours.

blocked.species: Ficus macrophylla (Palazzo Pantelleria, Piazza Giovanni Meli)
blocked.reason: MASAF register, girth 1010cm, height 17m, a genuinely large fig and previously left as an open lead. Researched this pass (2026-08-19): the tree grows in the internal/inner courtyard of Palazzo Pantelleria-Varvaro, a privately owned historic palace. Multiple sources describe visiting as guided tours led personally by the owner ('il padrone di casa', e.g. palermotoday.it's 'Palazzo Pantelleria Varvaro apre le porte, visite guidate in compagnia del padrone di casa', 10 May 2026) rather than standing public access. This is a courtyard of a dwelling under hard rule 10, which does not bend regardless of the tree's quality: BLOCKED, not a lead. If a future pass finds evidence of regular, ticketed, standing public opening hours (not a one-off event), revisit.

blocked.species: Washingtonia filifera / Palma californiana (Via Claudio Monteverdi)
blocked.reason: MASAF register, girth 235cm, height 16m. Researched this pass (2026-08-20): lasiciliainrete.it's page for this exact tree is a register republication only (photo credited simply 'google', no independent facts), same non-source pattern as the Ucciardone platano and Piazza Virgilio fig leads above. More importantly, palermolive.it (Palermo, quartiere Malaspina-Palagonia local news) describes Via Claudio Monteverdi as a street lined with roughly thirty Washingtonia filifera palms planted in a row, with a recurring hazard of falling fronds/branches. Nothing found distinguishes the one register-designated palm from the other ~29 visually identical palms on the same street, no signage or marker. This is the La Rambla problem: an avenue, not a single collectible point with one obvious place to stand. BLOCKED as an avenue entry, not a lead, unless a future pass finds the tree individually marked or otherwise made identifiable (in which case it would still need a real second source, since this one has none).
